title: Check duplicate records
summary: A duplicate is a repeated record. Some repeats are mistakes, but repeated events can also be real. Use a suitable identifier before removing anything.
introduction: A duplicate is a repeated record. Some repeats are mistakes, but repeated events can also be real. Use a suitable identifier before removing anything. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A duplicate is a repeated record. Some repeats are mistakes, but repeated events can also be real. Use a suitable identifier before removing anything.

blocks.code:
events = [{"id": "a", "type": "story"}, {"id": "a", "type": "story"}, {"id": "b", "type": "story"}]
ids = [row["id"] for row in events]
print(len(ids), len(set(ids)))
blocks.title: Check duplicate records

blocks.text: The output is 3 2. There are three rows and two distinct event IDs. This suggests a repeated event ID worth checking.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Explain why two different story borrowings should not be merged just because their type matches.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Do not remove all repeated values when separate events can share them.
